$comment: Structured claims registry. Validated offline by scripts/check_claims.py; field meanings and the human-review process are in docs/EVIDENCE.md ('Claims registry'). 'verification' says HOW a claim was checked, using the kinds defined in scripts/check_freshness.py VERIFICATION_KINDS; a static-pattern match is never verification. skill: null means the claim backs repo tooling (e.g. a known_stale_patterns entry in schema/freshness_policy.json) rather than one skill.

claims.claim: faiss IndexFlatIP.search pads ids with -1 (scores -3.4028235e38) when k exceeds ntotal
claims.evidence: tests/examples/test_rag_pipeline.py::TestFakeIndexMatchesFaiss::test_search_semantics_match and tests/examples/test_rag_pipeline.py::TestRagPipelineRealFaiss (real faiss-cpu); also observed directly: IndexFlatIP(4) holding 2 vectors, search(k=5) returned I=[[0, 1, -1, -1, -1]], D=[[1, 0, -3.4028235e+38 x3]]
claims.notes: The FAQ entry ('What does it mean when a search returns -1 ids?') states the -1 fill for IndexIVF/IndexHNSW; the IndexFlatIP case and the -3.4028235e38 (-FLT_MAX) score come from the runtime test, not the FAQ. Other faiss versions not tested.

claims.claim: sklearn.cross_validation is not importable in current scikit-learn (backs the 'sklearn-cross-validation' known_stale_patterns entry)
claims.evidence: tests/test_check_freshness.py::TestKnownStaleApisStillGone::test_sklearn_cross_validation_gone (skips when scikit-learn is not installed); re-run on 2026-10-29 with scikit-learn 1.9.0 (global Python 3.13.2, Windows), OK
claims.notes: Only absence in the tested version is runtime-verified. The v0.18 release notes (read 2026-10-27) deprecate sklearn.cross_validation in favour of sklearn.model_selection. The removal release was read from source, not from release notes (they do not mention it): sklearn/cross_validation.py exists at git tag 0.19.2 and is absent at tag 0.20.0 (raw.githubusercontent.com, read 2026-10-29 by an agent), so it was removed in 0.20.

claims.claim: tf.contrib does not exist in TensorFlow 2.x: tensorflow 2.21.0 has no tf.contrib attribute and 'import tensorflow.contrib' raises ImportError (backs the 'tensorflow-contrib' known_stale_patterns entry)
claims.evidence: tests/test_check_freshness.py::TestTensorflowContribGone::test_tf_contrib_not_importable; passed on 2026-10-29 (1 test, OK) in a scratch venv with tensorflow-cpu 2.21.0 from PyPI (PYTHONPATH=tests python -m unittest tests.test_check_freshness.TestTensorflowContribGone)
claims.notes: The TensorFlow 2.0.0 release notes (GitHub release v2.0.0, published 2019-09-30, read 2026-10-29) say 'tf.contrib has been deprecated, and functionality has been either migrated to the core TensorFlow API, to an ecosystem project such as tensorflow/addons or tensorflow/io, or removed entirely.' Only tensorflow-cpu 2.21.0 was run (scratch venv, Windows 11, Python 3.13.2); no CI job installs TensorFlow, so the test skips there. Absence in 2.0-2.20 is from the release notes, not executed. So the STALE verdict this claim backs rests on one local run that no CI job repeats; re-run the test in a TensorFlow venv when refreshing last_reviewed. A second check, tests/integration/test_tensorflow.py::TestKerasSamePadding::test_tf_contrib_does_not_exist, passed 2026-10-29 against tensorflow 2.21.0 / keras 3.15.1 (CPU, Windows 11, CPython 3.13.2, opt-in ML_AI_SKILLS_INTEGRATION_TF=1, not CI).

claims.claim: OpenAI text-davinci-* completion models are retired (backs the 'openai-text-davinci' known_stale_patterns entry)
claims.evidence: model knowledge at authoring time. Re-check attempted 2026-10-29 by an agent, not a person: platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations and openai.com failed DNS from the test machine, the WebFetch tool refused both OpenAI doc domains, and web.archive.org answered 403/429 to urllib, so no primary statement of the retirement was read
claims.notes: Indirect hint only, not proof of retirement: openai-python main src/openai/types/completion_create_params.py (read on GitHub 2026-10-29) lists only gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, davinci-002 and babbage-002 as known completion model ids. Because the claim is unverified, check_freshness.py reports matches of the 'openai-text-davinci' STALE pattern as REVIEW_DUE (not failing CI). Needs human-review against OpenAI's deprecations page; record the URL and access date when done.
